intro:
By this sign: the Komuch offensive

June 8th, 1918

Samara fell this morning. Czechoslovak battalions took the Volga bridge before the demolition party reached it, and a Committee of Constituent Assembly deputies has declared itself the government of Russia.

It has five deputies, a press and no soldiers of its own; by November Kolchak's officers will make that plain to it. Until then it has the railway, and the railway is the front. Hold Simbirsk, Melekess, Stavropol and Syzran, and take Samara back if it can be done.

briliant.text:
The four towns are held and the line between them is ours. We did not get Samara back - the bridgehead was reinforced across the river faster than we could close it, and a frontal attack over that bridge with the troops available would have cost the detachment and bought nothing.

The Eastern Front is being organised properly at last: Vatsetis is forming it into armies with staffs and a supply service instead of detachments that answer to whoever raised them. What we have given him is a front that still exists to be organised.

The railway line has gone with the towns on it. The detachments that were holding it are coming north as best they can, most of them without their guns.

The Volga from Syzran to Melekess is theirs, and Kazan is now the front line.

intro:
The gold in the vaults: Kazan

August 4th, 1918

Six hundred million roubles of the Imperial reserve lie in the vaults under this city. That, and not the map, is why Kappel's column is coming here.

Whoever walks out with them pays for a year of war, so Kazan cannot be traded for space. Kappel has three thousand men and two gunboats; the 5th Army is three days old. Hold the Kremlin, the academy and the river crossings.

briliant.text:
Kazan is held, the vaults are intact, and the flotilla base downstream has been burned out from the land side.

Trotsky's train is at Sviyazhsk and the Fifth Army has been given a spine in a week: field courts, commissars in every regiment, and reinforcements coming up the line from Moscow. The gold stays where it is until it can be moved under guard.

The Committee's people are calling this their high-water mark in the newspapers. They are about to be right.

Our army has fallen back on Sviyazhsk. Trotsky's train arrived there this morning and the first thing off it was a field tribunal.

intro:
The Committee comes apart: Samara and Syzran

September 18th, 1918

Kazan was retaken on the tenth and Simbirsk on the twelfth. The mobilised peasants will not fight for the Committee, and the Czechoslovaks have decided they are going home.

Samara and Syzran are the last of it. The Committee's staff and treasury are loading at Krotovka for Ufa, and every column that gets out will be back in the line in the spring under Kolchak. Take both towns and hold Simbirsk behind them.

briliant.text:
Samara and Syzran are ours. The Committee of Members of the Constituent Assembly ceased to govern anything at about two o'clock this afternoon.

Much of their staff got away east - the trains at Krotovka were loaded and moving before our cavalry reached the yard, and a railway is a hard thing to catch. What did not get away was the People's Army, which has stopped existing as a formation. The Volga is Soviet from Nizhny to Astrakhan.

In Omsk, meanwhile, they have decided that committees were the problem. There is talk of a Supreme Ruler.

intro:
Thirty below: the winter blow at Ufa

January 6th, 1919

There is a Supreme Ruler now, by his own proclamation: Kolchak took Omsk in November by arresting the Committee's ministers, and the Entente recognised it by going on unloading rifles for him.

Behind his front the atamans are already hanging people along the railway, which will cost him an army - but not this winter. His first stroke is at Ufa, where the 5th Army holds a hundred and fifty versts with nine thousand men at thirty below. Hold Ufa and the approaches.

briliant.text:
Ufa is held and the forming-up area at Iglino was broken up before their main body could use it.

The front will still be shortened. Not because of this sector: the Perm direction has gone - the 3rd Army lost eighteen thousand men and the city on Christmas Eve - and a line that holds in the centre while its right is walked round is a line that gets encircled. We go back on the Ufa river in good order and with the army intact.

A commission from Moscow is on its way to find out what happened at Perm. Stalin and Dzerzhinsky, they say.

Perm went a fortnight ago. The whole Urals front is now a line drawn on a map in Moscow and not much else.

intro:
Khanzhin's breakthrough: the spring offensive

March 1st, 1919

Khanzhin's Western Army came out of the thaw at the junction of the 5th and 1st Armies with three to one on the axis of attack. Behind it Gaida is driving on Vyatka.

If Gaida joins hands with the interventionists at Archangel, the northern half of the Republic is cut off from Moscow. Hold Belebei, Tuymazy, Abdulino, Sterlitamak and Meleuz; Ufa behind their front is their railhead.

briliant.text:
The five towns are still ours and their timetable is a fortnight behind.

That fortnight is the whole value of what was done here. The Central Committee has declared the Eastern Front the decisive front; Frunze is forming a southern group at Buzuluk out of everything the Republic can scrape together, and every day their offensive spends grinding against these towns is a day that group gets stronger and their own flank gets longer.

lose.text:
The junction was broken open and the towns went one after another. Their cavalry is between our two armies and there is no continuous front left on this sector.

Frunze's group at Buzuluk will have to be committed early, into a battle it did not choose.

intro:
The drive for the Volga: the spring offensive

March 14th, 1919

They have not stopped, and there is nothing behind this sector to stop them with. Khanzhin is driving for the Volga on a front too wide for his own supply.

He has been told the river must be reached before the Southern Front opens, and an army in that much of a hurry pays for every verst. There is no counterattack in these orders: a clock, and the line of towns from Belebei to Sterlitamak still ours when it stops.

briliant.text:
The line is still on the map and the towns named in my orders are still ours. Their leading regiments have outrun their own trains and are living off the villages, which in this province is the fastest way to lose a village.

Frunze's group is complete at Buzuluk. The southern group attacks in April.

lose.text:

intro:
The ring at Orenburg

April 17th, 1919

Dutov's Cossacks have besieged Orenburg on and off for a year. Without it their Host has no capital and no junction.

We hold it because it is the only rail link to Turkestan - cut it and Central Asia is on its own for the rest of the war. The garrison is the town: railwaymen, the Kirghiz and Tatar detachments, a workers' regiment. There will be no relief; the relieving force has gone to Buzuluk, because Frunze is about to attack. Hold the ring.

briliant.text:
The ring held. The road to Turkestan is open and the trains are running again, which means grain and cotton for the Republic and ammunition for Frunze.

Dutov has been drawing regiments off Kolchak's own flank to sit outside this town for a year. Long may he continue.

intro:
Frunze attacks: Belebei

May 15th, 1919

Frunze's southern group has broken the Western Army at Buguruslan and Bugulma. The initiative on this front has changed hands for the first time since January.

Khanzhin is trying to reform on the Belebei position with the old People's Army under a new name. Everything depends on hitting that position before it becomes one: Chapayev's 25th Division goes in first, and four turns is what makes this a rout instead of a battle.

briliant.text:
All four in the time allowed. The Volga Corps has been broken up as a formation and its trains are ours, and the road to Ufa is open.

Their spring offensive is finished. From here the Eastern Front does not defend.

victory.text:

lose.text:
We took the ground and took too long doing it. Their corps got back across the Belaya with its artillery and will be waiting for us on the far bank.

intro:
The tide turns: Chistopol

May 26th, 1919

North of this sector Gaida's Siberian Army is still pushing on Vyatka and has not understood that the army on its left has collapsed.

Take Bugulma and the Azanakayevo junction now and that whole northern group is fighting with a hole where its flank used to be. Fail, and their reserves come south and it is their offensive again - aimed at the Volga crossings, and fought for in front of Kazan.

briliant.text:
Bugulma and the junction are ours. Gaida's flank is open and he has finally been told to stop.

The front headquarters has confirmed the next objective and it is the one everybody has been waiting for: across the Belaya, and Ufa.

victory.text:

The initiative has gone with them. Kazan is being put into a state of defence and I am ordered there tonight.

intro:
Twice in one year: Kazan

June 10th, 1919

The May attack was held, and the counterstroke has carried them back onto the Volga. Kazan is the front line again.

The front is being rebuilt around this city while it is held: every division that comes up the line arrives because Kazan was still ours when it started loading. Hold the Kremlin, the academy and the crossings to the last turn.

briliant.text:
Kazan is held and their thrust has broken on it. Their army has spent the reserves it brought south and has nothing behind them.

The crisis is over. The front headquarters is putting the offensive back together on the old axis, and my orders send me east again - to the Belaya and Ufa, where this should have gone a month ago.

lose.text:

intro:
Where it all began: Samara

July 14th, 1919

A year and a month since the Czechoslovaks took this bridge, and it is being argued over again. Their advance down the Volga has been slowed, not stopped.

Front headquarters is shuttling staffs between three threatened directions by rail, which is what happens when a front has more axes than reserves. This group will not be reinforced. Hold Samara, Simbirsk and Syzran; Melekess and Krotovka are their staging points.

briliant.text:
The crossings are ours and their staging areas have been cleared. The Volga line holds.

The offensive can be restarted on the proper axis. I am ordered east to rejoin the drive on Ufa.

victory.text:

lose.text:
Samara has gone. The bridge was blown behind the last of our columns, which is the one thing on my list that got done properly.

The staff is being moved north to Vyatka. So am I.

intro:
Cutting the Republic in two: Vyatka

October 20th, 1919

Gaida is gone - dismissed in the summer, and since then he has tried to overthrow his own government in Vladivostok - but the Siberian Army's northern drive has been picked up by someone else.

It still wants Vyatka and a junction with the interventionists from Archangel. If they meet, the Republic is cut in half along the Northern Dvina. Hold the Vyatka sectors and Karavayevy; Vakhrushi is their forward railhead.

briliant.text:
Vyatka holds and the two halves of their northern plan are still two hundred versts apart. The British at Archangel are loading their own transports; they will not be coming south for anybody.

The front can be restored on the main axis. East, to Ufa.

The city sectors were lost one by one over four days. What is left of the group is going south-west on the Kotelnich road.

The next place they can be stopped is Saratov, which tells you how far this has gone.

intro:
The Black Baron: Saratov

November 13th, 1919

Wrangel's Caucasus Army has come up the Volga from Tsaritsyn to shake hands with Kolchak's people.

A junction of the two White fronts on the middle Volga is the one thing both commands have wanted all year and never arranged, largely because neither will serve under the other. They are not to arrange it here. Hold the Saratov sectors and Atkarsk; Volsk is where the link is being tried.

briliant.text:
They have not linked up. Saratov is ours, the railway west is open, and the two White armies remain what they have been all year: two armies.

Front headquarters is turning the offensive back east. Ufa next, and this time properly.

victory.text:

I am ordered to Ryazan with what I can bring out.

intro:
The junction before Moscow: Ryazan

December 12th, 1919

Ryazan is not a front-line town. It is where the roads from the south and the east meet before Moscow, which is why a group made of other people's spare regiments is standing in it in December.

If this line goes there is one more behind it, and then there is Moscow. Hold Ryazan, Kolomna and Kashira. Their forward group has come up at Venev on the Tula road, and it is worth more to us than to them yet.

briliant.text:
The junction is held and their forward group has been pushed off the Tula road. The reserves that were forming behind us have not had to be spent covering a retreat, which means they can be used for something.

The front is going over to the offensive again on the eastern axis. My group entrains tomorrow.

intro:
Sixty versts from Moscow: Klin

December 30th, 1919

Klin is on the Petrograd railway sixty versts from Moscow. There is nothing behind this one.

Everything the Republic could scrape together in a fortnight is here: the courses cadets, two workers' regiments from the Moscow factories, the internationalist battalion, and regiments retreating since Saratov that are being asked to stop today. Hold Klin and the four villages until the clock runs out.

briliant.text:
It held. Their attack has stopped in front of Klin and this morning their forward units were reported moving back.

They cannot stay where they are: a front that long, in winter, at the end of a single railway with partisans on it, does not hold together once it stops moving forward. The reserves that were built up behind this line are intact and they are going east.

Back to the proper war. Ufa is in my orders and I have been waiting a long time to read that word again.

intro:
The May counterattack: Zhitomir

May 19th, 1920

The Polish armies took Kiev on the seventh. The 12th and 14th Armies were pushed back over the Dnieper and are being put together again behind it.

Warsaw's object here is a client state under Petliura, bought last month with eastern Galicia and western Volhynia. Attack now: the Western Front opened in Belorussia on the fourteenth, and every Polish division kept here this fortnight is one that does not entrain north. Take Korosten, Zwiahel, Zhitomir and Kazatin; hold Malin and Fastov.

briliant.text:
Korosten, Zwiahel, Zhitomir and Kazatin are ours and the junctions between them are working. Malin and Fastov were never seriously threatened.

What this buys is not territory. It is the four Polish divisions that spent this fortnight in Volhynia instead of going north against the Western Front, and a rail net that the 1st Cavalry Army will detrain onto when it finishes its march from the Kuban.

The decision on this front will not be taken here. It will be taken in the first week of June, in the seam at Samhorodok, by an army that is still on the road today. Our part was to see that the seam is still there when it arrives.

intro:
Across the Belaya: Ufa

May 29th, 1919

The Western Army is broken, and the town it has supplied itself from all spring is on the far bank of a wide river with one bridge.

Chapayev's 25th Division crosses on rafts north of the city; the rest of the group goes for the Chishmy junction to cut the line out from under the garrison. No reserve and no second attempt - twelve turns to take Ufa, and their rearguard has been allowed the same twelve.

briliant.text:
Ufa is ours and the Chishmy junction with it. Their army went east along the Zlatoust line at night with what it could carry.

The Urals are open. Chapayev was gassed from the air over the crossing and refused to be taken off the field; he is in the line today.

Next is the passes, and after the passes, Siberia.

intro:
The house on Voznesensky Lane: Ekaterinburg

July 12th, 1919

The 2nd and 3rd Armies are over the northern Urals. Ekaterinburg is the junction of everything on this front and the last real city before Siberia.

Their evacuation began before our guns were in range: six columns of staff, treasury and archives on the Tyumen line, and what is in them decides what anyone can prove afterwards about the house on Voznesensky Lane. Take the city and let nothing reach the eastern exit.

briliant.text:
Ekaterinburg is taken. The works are intact - they had the demolition charges laid and no time to fire them.

Sokolov's investigation papers, or what our people could stop of them, are with the tribunal. I have read enough of the summary to be glad the rest is somebody else's work.

The road east is the Trans-Siberian and there is very little on it now that can stop an army.

The 3rd Army has been badly cut about doing it and the pursuit will have to wait for it to be made up. The front headquarters has asked me some sharp questions and they are fair ones.

intro:
Both shoulders at once: Chelyabinsk

July 25th, 1919

The 5th Army came through the passes into Chelyabinsk yesterday. Keeping it is evidently a different question from taking it.

Kolchak's staff planned exactly this: let the Reds in, close from Miasskoye and from the north, and destroy an army in a street it thinks it owns. The city rose to help take it - the railway workshops turned out three regiments in a week. Hold the town and its approaches to the last turn.

briliant.text:
Both pincers were broken and the city is ours. Their counterstroke was their last army reserve in the Urals and it has been spent.

There is no natural line between here and the Tobol. The pursuit goes on into Siberia.

lose.text:
The pincers closed north of the city and the army had to fight its way west out of a town it had taken. The workshop regiments covered the withdrawal and most of them did not come out.

The Urals will have to be done again.

intro:
They are not finished: the Tobol (I)

September 1st, 1919

Kolchak's armies have been reorganised behind the Tobol. Dieterichs combed out the rear areas, the Siberian Cossacks are mobilised wholesale, and their staff counted correctly: our divisions are at half strength, six hundred versts from railhead.

The reports that said this enemy was finished were wrong, and this is the bill for them. The blow has fallen on the left, where the Cossack cavalry has open steppe. Hold the line of villages; Petropavlovsk is what all of it is a step towards.

briliant.text:
The line held through the whole of their effort. They have put in their last mobilised reserves against these villages and they have not moved us off them.

Our own reinforcements are coming up the line at last. The counterstroke on the Tobol is being prepared and it will not have to start from behind a river.

lose.text:
We were pushed back off the villages and over the Tobol. Their cavalry is loose on the steppe behind our left.

The line will have to be restored on the river, and restoring it is the next task.

intro:
An offensive running on nothing: the Tobol (II)

September 25th, 1919

Their offensive is a month old and running on nothing.

Every recruit put into the line this month came from a village that is now sending its sons to the partisans instead, and their supply comes down one railway with the Siberian detachments sitting on it. They have gained ground and lost the army that gained it. Hold Kurgan, Chashinskiy, Vargashi and the Tobol crossing.

briliant.text:
The Tobol line is ours and their forward groups have been broken up on the near bank. That is the end of the last offensive Kolchak's armies will ever mount.

From here it is pursuit, and the only questions are how fast we can move and how much of Siberia rises in front of us. Omsk is four hundred versts away and their government is already loading its trains.

We are back over the Tobol and holding the far bank. Their groups east of the river are intact.

It has cost them more than it has cost us, which is true and is no consolation while the line is where it is.

intro:
The bridge over the Ob: Novonikolayevsk

December 7th, 1919

Omsk fell without a fight three weeks ago. Their government left by train and their army left on foot, and the two have not been in the same place since.

In front of us is the Great Siberian Ice March: half a million people, the remains of three armies, their families and the typhus, moving east down one railway in December. Novonikolayevsk is the bridge over the Ob - take it and the column east is cut off from the column west.

briliant.text:
The bridge is taken. Thirty thousand prisoners and more typhus cases than anyone can count; the town's hospitals were full before we arrived and the retreating command left them as they were.

The Fifth Army is ordered to go on to Krasnoyarsk. There is a rising there already - the garrison has arrested its own officers - and the partisan armies of the Yenisei are on the railway ahead of us.

The bridge was blown and the column east of the Ob got clear. We hold the west bank and the typhus wards.

They will be caught somewhere further east, by us or by the winter.

intro:
The town took itself: Krasnoyarsk

January 4th, 1920

Krasnoyarsk has taken itself: the garrison arrested its own commander on the last day of December, and the town is held by a revolutionary committee, the railway workers and Shchetinkin's partisans.

Our leading divisions are four days behind. Kappel's column is coming down the line - what is left of three armies, on foot, in forty degrees of frost, with nothing to lose. Hold the city and Drokino with what is here. The partisans know this country as we do not; they are allies.

briliant.text:
The city is held. Sixty thousand men laid down their arms in and around it over three days - most of them conscripts who had been waiting for somewhere to stop.

Part of the column went round us to the north, over the Yenisei ice and into the taiga, and is heading for Irkutsk along the river. Kappel is with them. In this weather, on that route, the frost will do most of what we would have had to do.

The Fifth Army goes on east. So do I.

lose.text:
They came through the town. The committee's detachments and the partisans fought in the streets for two days and the column went east over their dead.

It is not finished. There is one more place on this railway where it can be finished, and it is Irkutsk.

intro:
The last of it: Irkutsk

January 27th, 1920

The Political Centre rose here at the end of December and handed the city, and the Supreme Ruler, to the Revolutionary Committee. Kolchak is in the prison, and so is what is left of the gold.

Out of the taiga comes what survived the march: Kappel died on the road, and Voitsekhovsky has demanded the city, the prisoner and a contribution. Semyonov is east of the lake, and the Baikal ice is the only way past. Hold Irkutsk and Listvennichnoye.

briliant.text:
Irkutsk is held. The column went round the city in the end - over the Baikal ice, in February, in a wind that took more of them than we did - and what reached Transbaikalia reached it as a crowd and not as an army.

Kolchak was shot on the seventh of February by order of the Revolutionary Committee, with Voitsekhovsky's guns within a day's march. They put him and Pepelyaev through the ice of the Ushakovka.

The Eastern Front is finished. Two years ago I was a commander of a detachment on a railway with four towns on it and no orders; tonight I am writing a report in Irkutsk and the line behind me runs unbroken to Moscow. The Far East is not ours yet and there is a buffer republic being argued about in the newspapers, but that is politics and somebody else's work.

I am going home by train. It will take eleven days and I intend to sleep for all of them.
